 Ensuring the supply of essential goods during the rainy season and floods.
 HNN - In addition to the proactive efforts of businesses, Hue City is strengthening its review of plans for stockpiling and distributing essential goods, especially in areas at risk of being isolated by floods; at the same time, it is controlling the market, contributing to ensuring supply and stabilizing prices when natural disasters occur.
 Huế ngày nay • 31/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 
 GO! Hue supermarket staff inspect and arrange goods in reserve for the flood and storm season. 
 Proactive stockpiling 
 Having traded at Dong Ba Market for over 50 years, Ms. Thai Thi Qua has extensive experience in preparing goods before the rainy season and floods. Since September, she has imported approximately 5 tons of essential goods, such as flour, sticky rice, and processed foods; and proactively adjusted her inventory according to market demand.
 "Experience from previous years shows that goods can be scarce during the rainy season and floods, and transportation is also difficult. Therefore, this year I proactively imported more goods from multiple sources to build up reserves," Ms. Qua shared.
 According to the Dong Ba Market Management Board, traders are currently stockpiling about 50 tons of food and essential goods, mainly rice, sticky rice, cooking oil, and dried food, ready to serve the people when floods occur.
 According to Ms. Le Thi Kim Chi, Deputy Head of the Dong Ba Market Management Board, the unit is intensifying its efforts to promote, encourage, and guide traders to stockpile essential goods, especially food, in order to mitigate the risk of shortages and sudden price increases during the rainy season.
 At GO! Hue supermarket, the amount of goods stockpiled for the rainy and stormy season is estimated at around 70-80 tons, including 5,000 boxes of instant noodles, 1,000 boxes of milk, 1,000 boxes of bottled water, about 3,000 boxes of biscuits, dried food, and other essential items. The amount of rice in reserve is estimated at around 250kg.
 You may also like “The supermarket is committed to supplying essential goods such as rice, milk, cooking oil, flashlights, and other necessities to the Department of Industry and Trade. Based on that, we coordinate with suppliers and procurement centers to develop ordering and inventory plans to ensure supply when demand increases,” said Ms. Pham Thi Thu Trang, Director of GO! Hue supermarket.
 According to Hue City's plan, the amount of essential goods to be stockpiled at the city level is determined at two levels. The minimum level includes 10 tons of rice, 10,000 cartons of instant noodles, 5,000 packs of pasteurized fresh milk (each pack containing 4 boxes, 180ml/box), and 100,000 bottles of 500ml drinking water. At the maximum level, the amount of these items is doubled. For other necessities, the amount to be stockpiled is based on the registration of businesses. At the ward/commune level, the maximum reserve level includes 331.124 tons of rice, 39,007 cartons of instant noodles, 913,112 bottles of 500ml drinking water, and more than 5 tons of other necessities such as dried food, dried rations, cooking oil, and canned food.
 Ensuring supply and controlling prices. 
 According to the Department of Industry and Trade, 15 businesses have so far committed to supplying goods to people in the event of natural disasters, with the amount of goods registered for reserve exceeding the city's requirements. The maximum reserve includes 129,500 kg of rice, 68,500 cartons of instant noodles, 191,500 packs of UHT milk, 439,700 bottles of bottled water (500ml and 350ml), and 14,880 cartons of biscuits and dried food.
 Along with preparing supplies, the city is strengthening inspections of response plans in localities, especially in mountainous areas at risk of being isolated. From October 12 to 15, the working group from the Department of Industry and Trade inspected the following commune clusters: Nam Dong, Long Quang, Khe Tre; A Luoi 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; Phu Loc, Chan May - Lang Co and Loc An.
 During the inspection, the delegation requested that localities develop disaster prevention and control plans that are realistic; arrange convenient collection and storage points for goods to facilitate reception and distribution when transportation is disrupted. At the same time, they were asked to review the transportation and communication systems, and generators; and supplement milk, drinking water, and food according to the needs of each target group.
 You may also like The industry and trade sector also coordinates with local authorities and businesses to closely monitor supply and demand, proactively coordinate goods, strengthen market inspection and supervision, and promptly handle acts of speculation and exploitation of natural disasters to unreasonably increase prices.
 Mr. Phan Hung Son, Deputy Director of the Department of Industry and Trade, said that the unit has directed market management forces to closely monitor the area, providing complete data on goods sources so that localities can proactively purchase and mobilize supplies when natural disasters occur. At the same time, they are strengthening inspections and strictly handling cases of exploiting floods to raise prices, protecting consumer rights.
